acceptance: Lock values independently recomputed and verified (both wheel URLs hashed).
Required-context and caller-input check recorded (ruleset id, contexts, inputs).
Merged to Theseus main with hosted SHIP + green checks + independent review SHIP on the final head (recorded).
The next Theseus PR after the merge shows the new verdict body and thread format and its review-gate passes on SHIP (link recorded).
Minimise-flag decision for Theseus's own policy recorded (if applicable).
context: Part of theseus-review-output-format-20261110. Added on the owner's decision of 2026-11-10.
description:
Theseus reviews its own pull requests with a pinned release: .github/theseus-lock.json is v0.2.4 and both callers (.github/workflows/review-verdict.yml, review-gate.yml) use @8635dc7. Theseus PRs will not show the new output until this lock is promoted. Promote it to release B with the same lock procedure BenchBox uses (version, source_commit, workflow_sha, source_sha256, delta_sha256 from the current v0.2.4 lock, artifact sha256 and URLs; same SHA in both callers' `uses:` and `with.theseus_ref`).
The jump from v0.2.4 brings every intervening change (classifier, protocol, evals, cleanup and legacy removal, v0.2.7 multi-base gating, oracle mirror removal): check the Theseus main ruleset still requires only contexts the new release posts (review-gate from App 5620429) and that the callers pass every input/secret the release's reusable workflows declare as required.
Decision gate: if theseus-review-minimize-superseded-20261110 shipped, the owner decides whether Theseus's own policy enables minimising after this lock merges (separate policy PR).
Guardrails: lock and caller change, so G7 applies in full: hosted SHIP + green checks + independent review of the exact final head; no ruleset change without recording before/after captures; no live model calls.
